body:
We used an offline VM running a copy of our Agie Classic Cut 2S machine control. We imported the CAMCraft punch with a reentrant notch. GRAFICHECK preserved the notch on all four passes. The plotted apex positions matched the intersections of the offset faces. FORMALCHECK reported zero job errors.

All controller runs were offline. No physical cut was made.

Port to the current frame. New head `1962fd5dc`.

- The branch merges the ported #2964 head `4a94c23ce`. It does not use the old setup writer of this branch. The SBL comes from `agie_setup.rs` (zero erosion steps, `ID_PUNCH c_punch`, 1.0 mm separation).
- Conflicts:
  - `agie_profile.rs`: the contour now comes from `closed_vertical_prism`. The convex prism refusal is removed. The refusal texts use the new names of #3537.
  - `agie/contour.rs`: the convex refusal of #2955 is replaced by the reentrant reach check. The stock, miter and setup checks of #2964 and #2984 stay. The reach and the spacing use the rough offset of the selected thickness from `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`.
  - `agie/tests.rs`, `tests/agie_native.rs` and the user guide: both sides are kept.
- The spacing check moved to `agie/spacing.rs`. The reentrant tests moved to `agie/reentrant_tests.rs` and `tests/agie_native/reentrant.rs`. Each file stays under 400 lines.
- New tests pin the reach at each measured thickness and the zero-step SBL of the notched job.
- The gate result is in the PR body. The one red step is the known gpu clippy finding.
- The ported job was not imported on the offline control. Import `NOTCH20` on the control VM before machine use.

## Offline control import: NOTCH20, and the notch at 40 and 80 mm (2026-11-23)

The jobs came from head `30e6c4c3f` (the port stack #2955, #2964, #2968, #2969). This head contains the head `1962fd5dc` of this PR.

### Jobs

- `NOTCH20`: `examples/agie/notched-punch.camscript` without changes.
- `NOTCH40` and `NOTCH80`: the same script and mesh with the height, stock, WCS and `top_z` set to 40 or 80 mm. CamCraft accepted the 1 mm notch at both thicknesses.

Each receipt says `"working_steps_generated": false`.

### Procedure

- Emulated AGIEVISION CUT Classic S. A throwaway clone of the saved state `practice-color-ready`, reloaded before each job.
- Import of the ISO, then the SBL with its SBR, from a read-only floppy image. A host-side read of the guest disk confirmed the imported bytes.
- New piece from `Script Files`. FORMALCHECK with and without warnings. TECCUT assignment. GRAFICHECK. The plot file `1.J00` was copied out and read.

### Readings

| Reading | NOTCH20 | NOTCH40 | NOTCH80 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Work line after import | `CCB030[0]` | `CCB030[0]` | `CCB030[0]` |
| FORMALCHECK before TECCUT | `Technologie : te definiëren` only | the same | the same |
| TECCUT header | `Dia:0.25 H:20 Ra:0.30 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5` | `H:40`, the rest the same | `H:80`, the rest the same |
| Technology, pre-selected row | `estbca25nnn060b030020`, `0199 01.36 4` | `estbca25nnn060b030050`, `0241 00.68 4` | `estbca25nnn080b030070`, `0235 00.53 4` |
| Work line after TECCUT | `CCB030[4]` | `CCB030[4]` | `CCB030[4]` |
| Pass offsets (µm) | 245, 155, 140, 134 | 260, 170, 140, 130 | 266, 176, 143, 133 |
| FORMALCHECK after TECCUT | `geen fouten` | `geen fouten` | `geen fouten` |
| Warnings after TECCUT | `Uitgekozen opties : 131072`, `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` | the same | the same |

### Plot (`1.J00`)

NOTCH20:
- Start hole X-30 Y0. Entry at X-20 Y0 on the left face.
- Each pass has the seven faces of the punch. The notch is between X-10 and X10.
- The notch tip at X0 is at Y 9.2462 (Main), 9.1558 (Trim1), 9.1407 (Trim2) and 9.1347 (Trim3). These values agree with the readings of the old branch (9.246222, 9.155773, 9.140698, 9.134668) to 0.0001 mm.
- The main loop stops at Y1.000 on the left face and leaves a 1.000 mm separation.
- Each pass returns to X-30 Y0, the threading hole.

Notch tips at X0 at the other thicknesses:
- NOTCH40: Y 9.2613, 9.1708, 9.1407, 9.1306. Calculated from the offsets and the 1:10 slope: 9.2613, 9.1708, 9.1407, 9.1306.
- NOTCH80: Y 9.2673, 9.1769, 9.1437, 9.1337. Calculated: 9.2673, 9.1769, 9.1437, 9.1337.

### Result

NOTCH20 agrees with the expectation: zero steps at import, seven faces, the four notch tips, the 1 mm separation and the return to the threading hole. NOTCH40 and NOTCH80 also give zero steps, no FORMALCHECK error after TECCUT and the measured offsets of each thickness. I found no mismatch.

### Not checked

- No physical cut.
- Screenshots and the `.J00` files are in the local notes folder `agie-imports-20261123/NOTCH20`, `NOTCH40` and `NOTCH80`.

Goldens moved: none. I checked the new ISO lines against the nominal vertices.
The notched job's SBL matches the existing CCSEP20 golden byte for byte after the job-name replacement.
The author now reports offline control checks for the 20, 40 and 80 mm jobs in [this comment](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2968#issuecomment-7115465122).
The reported stack head is `30e6c4c3f`, which the author states contains this PR head.
I did not repeat the control VM checks. No physical cut was made in this review.

**Requested before merge**

1. **Process declaration** — `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md:149` changes a process file, but the PR body lacks `Process change: yes`.
   Add that line to the body. Current upstream `AGENTS.md:173` requires this declaration for each PR that changes a process file.
   The merge session sets the process version.
2. **Control instructions** — `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md:50` gives the 20 mm offsets for every supported thickness.
   For 40 mm stock, the offsets are `0.260, 0.170, 0.140, 0.130 mm`.
   For 80 mm stock, they are `0.266, 0.176, 0.143, 0.133 mm`.
   Point this step to the table row for the selected thickness.
   Keep all control checks consistent with `QN2_OFFSETS_UM` and the returned `controller_review`.

**Optional, non-blocking**

`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md:149` still describes convex punches only.
State the checked reentrant support and its limits there too.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

This PR goes back to draft. The branch takes the new #2964 head `3a29a5f9d` (it merges `main` at `44e6a8269` and the TECCUT guide fix) and the review fixes of `1962fd5dc`. A gate runs on the new head before the PR is ready again.

Reply to the [review of `1962fd5dc`](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2968). New head: `6443d4f09`.

1. **Process declaration.** The PR body now has the line `Process change: yes`. The PR does not change `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.
2. **Control instructions.** The merge of the #2964 head `3a29a5f9d` brings commit `92ca17909`. Step 3 of `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md` now points to the row of the selected stock thickness in the QN2 offsets table, in the order rough, trim 1, trim 2, trim 3. The 20 mm values stay only as an example. The table agrees with `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`, and `controller_review` names the four offsets of the same row.
3. **Optional: skill row.** Commit `6443d4f09` changes the Wire Contour row of `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The row now states the checked reentrant support and its limits: the reach of the rough offset of the selected thickness (0.002 mm), the corner joins on each segment, the spacing of nonadjacent faces and the exterior entry. A notch that fails a check is refused. The row links `docs/decisions/2956-agie-reentrant-punch.md`.

The new head also contains `main` at `44e6a8269` (#3219), through #2964. The files under `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/` did not change, and `agie_native` still compares the notched SBL with the `CCSEP20` golden file. Thus the posted bytes are the same as at `1962fd5dc`. The [control import record](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2968#issuecomment-7115465122) is linked in the body.

Gate on `6443d4f09`: batch plan, 1189 steps, 1 failed (`rotary_verify`, the known red of `main`, #3774), 0 stalled. Clippy is clean. The body has the details.

Ready for a re-check.
